The student wants to emphasize a difference between baking soda and baking powder.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: To make batters rise, bakers use chemical leavening agents such as baking soda and baking powder.
choices.B: Baking soda and baking powder are chemical leavening agents that, when mixed with other ingredients, cause carbon dioxide to be released within a batter.
choices.C: Baking soda is pure sodium bicarbonate, and honey is a type of acidic ingredient.
choices.D: To produce carbon dioxide within a liquid batter, baking soda needs to be mixed with an acidic ingredient, whereas baking powder does not.

explanation: The difference is the acid requirement: baking soda needs one, baking powder already contains it. A and B describe what the two share.

passage.t: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
The factors that affect clutch size (the number of eggs laid at one time) have been well studied in birds but not in lizards.
A team led by Shai Meiri of Tel Aviv University investigated which factors influence lizard clutch size.
Meiri’s team obtained clutch-size and habitat data for over 3,900 lizard species and analyzed the data with statistical models.

Larger clutch size was associated with environments in higher latitudes that have more seasonal change. Lizards in higher-latitude environments may lay larger clutches to take advantage of shorter windows of favorable conditions.
The student wants to emphasize the aim of the research study.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Researchers wanted to know which factors influence lizard egg clutch size because such factors have been well studied in birds but not in lizards.
choices.B: After they obtained data for over 3,900 lizard species, researchers determined that larger clutch size was associated with environments in higher latitudes that have more seasonal change.
choices.C: We now know that lizards in higher-latitude environments may lay larger clutches to take advantage of shorter windows of favorable conditions.
choices.D: Researchers obtained clutch-size and habitat data for over 3,900 lizard species and analyzed the data with statistical models.

explanation: The aim is why they undertook the study — clutch size was well understood in birds but not lizards. B and C give findings, and D the method.

passage.t: While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
Maika’i Tubbs is a Native Hawaiian sculptor and installation artist.
His work has been shown in the United States, Canada, Japan, and Germany, among other places.
Many of his sculptures feature discarded objects.
His work Erasure (2008) includes discarded audiocassette tapes and magnets.
His work Home Grown (2009) includes discarded pushpins, plastic plates and forks, and wood.
The student wants to emphasize a similarity between the two works.

stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Erasure (2008) uses discarded objects such as audiocassette tapes and magnets; Home Grown (2009), however, includes pushpins, plastic plates and forks, and wood.
choices.B: Tubbs’s work, which often features discarded objects, has been shown both within the United States and abroad.
choices.C: Like many of Tubbs’s sculptures, both Erasure and Home Grown include discarded objects: Erasure uses audiocassette tapes, and Home Grown uses plastic forks.
choices.D: Tubbs completed Erasure in 2008 and Home Grown in 2009.

explanation: The similarity is the use of discarded objects, and C names both works and the discarded items in each. A frames the same material as a contrast.

passage.t: Samuel Coleridge-Taylor was a prominent classical music composer from England who toured the US three times in the early 1900s. The child of a West African father and an English mother, Coleridge-Taylor emphasized his mixed- race ancestry. For example, he referred to himself as Anglo-African. ______ he incorporated the sounds of traditional African music into his classical music compositions.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In addition,
choices.B: Actually,
choices.C: However,
choices.D: Regardless,

explanation: Calling himself Anglo-African and incorporating African sounds into his music are two separate ways he emphasized his ancestry, so an additive transition is needed. There is no contrast (C, D) and no correction of a misunderstanding (B).

passage.t: In her poetry collection Thomas and Beulah, Rita Dove interweaves the titular characters’ personal stories with broader historical narratives. She places Thomas’s journey from the American South to the Midwest in the early 1900s within the larger context of the Great Migration. ______ Dove sets events from Beulah’s personal life against the backdrop of the US Civil Rights Movement.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Specifically,
choices.B: Thus,
choices.C: Regardless,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation: Both sentences give parallel examples of the same technique—setting a character's personal story against a historical backdrop. 'Similarly' signals that parallel. 'Specifically' would require narrowing, and 'Thus' would require a cause.

passage.t: In a heated debate in biogeography, the field is divided between dispersalists and vicariancists. ______ there are those who argue that dispersal is the most crucial determining factor in a species’ distribution, and those who insist that vicariance (separation due to geographic barriers) is. Biogeographer Isabel Sanmartín counts herself among neither.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Furthermore,
choices.B: By contrast,
choices.C: Similarly,
choices.D: That is,

explanation: The second sentence restates what 'divided between dispersalists and vicariancists' means, so a restating transition is needed. Nothing is added (A), contrasted (B), or compared (C).

passage.t: Most of the planets that have been discovered outside our solar system orbit G-type stars, like our Sun. In 2014, ______ researchers identified a planet orbiting KELT-9, a B-type star more than twice as massive and nearly twice as hot as the Sun. Called KELT-9b, it is one of the hottest planets ever discovered.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: likewise,
choices.B: however,
choices.C: therefore,
choices.D: for example,

explanation: Most such planets orbit G-type stars, but this one orbits a B-type star—a contrast with the norm just described. 'Likewise' and 'therefore' both signal agreement or consequence.

passage.t: In 1815, while in exile in Jamaica, Venezuelan revolutionary Simón Bolívar penned a letter praising England’s republican government and expressing hope that Latin American nations seeking independence from Spain might achieve something similar. The letter was addressed to a local merchant, Henry Cullen; ______ though, Bolívar’s goal was to persuade political leaders from England and Europe to support his cause.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: additionally,
choices.B: ultimately,
choices.C: accordingly,
choices.D: consequently,

explanation: The letter's nominal addressee is contrasted with Bolívar's real, final purpose, so 'ultimately' fits the 'though' already in the sentence. 'Additionally,' 'accordingly,' and 'consequently' would signal addition or cause, not the ultimate aim.

passage.t: The Babylonian king Hammurabi achieved much during his forty-year reign. He conquered all of Mesopotamia and built Babylon into one of the most powerful cities of the ancient world. Today, ______ he is mainly remembered for a code of laws inscribed on a seven-foot-tall block of stone: the Code of Hammurabi.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: therefore,
choices.B: likewise,
choices.C: however,
choices.D: for instance,

explanation: His conquests are contrasted with what he is actually remembered for today, so a contrast transition is required. 'Therefore' and 'likewise' signal consequence or similarity.

passage.t: Some members of the US Supreme Court have resisted calls to televise the court’s oral arguments, concerned that the participants would be tempted to perform for the cameras (and thus lower the quality of the discourse). ______ the justices worry that most viewers would not even watch the full deliberations, only short clips that could be misinterpreted and mischaracterized.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: However,
choices.B: Additionally,
choices.C: In comparison,
choices.D: For example,

explanation: The clipped-viewing worry is a second concern added to the performing-for-cameras worry, so an additive transition fits. It is not a contrast (A), a comparison (C), or an instance of the first concern (D).

passage.t: Award-winning travel writer Linda Watanabe McFerrin considers the background research she conducts on destinations featured in her travel books to be its own reward. ______ McFerrin admits to finding the research phase of her work just as fascinating and engaging as exploring a location in person.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: By contrast,
choices.B: Likewise,
choices.C: Besides,
choices.D: In fact,

explanation: The second sentence confirms and intensifies the claim that research is its own reward, so 'In fact' fits. 'By contrast' reverses the idea, and 'Likewise' would require a second, separate item.

passage.t: In 1873, Spanish scientist Santiago Ramón y Cajal observed that brain fibers have distinct boundaries with clear end points, a finding that went against earlier assumptions about the brain. ______ scientists had assumed that the brain was a continuous web of fused fibers, not a vast network of distinct, individual cells.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: However,
choices.B: Previously,
choices.C: As a result,
choices.D: Likewise,

explanation: The sentence describes the 'earlier assumptions' the finding overturned, so a transition marking earlier time is needed. 'However' and 'As a result' misstate the relationship.

passage.t: For years, biologists have experimented with using grime-eating bacteria rather than harsh chemicals to clean artworks, and results have been impressive overall. ______ these bacterial strains—which can metabolize centuries’ worth of oil, glue, dirt, and other surface impurities without creating harmful byproducts—have proven more effective than traditional chemical cleaning methods.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: However,
choices.B: In many cases,
choices.C: As a result,
choices.D: Additionally,

explanation: 'impressive overall' is narrowed to the specific circumstances in which the bacteria outperform chemicals, so a qualifying transition fits. 'However' would signal contrast, and 'As a result' a cause-effect link that isn't present.

passage.t: In 1968, US Congressman John Conyers introduced a bill to establish a national holiday in honor of Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. The bill didn’t make it to a vote, but Conyers was determined. He teamed up with Shirley Chisholm, the first Black woman to be elected to Congress, and they resubmitted the bill every session for the next fifteen years.
______ in 1983, the bill passed.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Instead,
choices.B: Likewise,
choices.C: Finally,
choices.D: Additionally,

explanation: After fifteen years of resubmission, the bill's 1983 passage is the culmination of the sequence, so 'Finally' fits. 'Instead,' 'Likewise,' and 'Additionally' do not mark the end of a long effort.

passage.t: It has long been thought that humans first crossed a land bridge into the Americas approximately 13,000 years ago. ______ based on radiocarbon dating of samples uncovered in Mexico, a research team recently suggested that humans may have arrived more than 30,000 years ago—much earlier than previously thought.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: As a result,
choices.B: Similarly,
choices.C: However,
choices.D: In conclusion,

explanation: The recent finding of 30,000 years contradicts the long-held 13,000-year figure, so a contrast transition is required.

passage.t: Researchers believe that pieces of hull found off Oregon’s coast are from a Spanish cargo ship that was lost in 1697. Stories passed down among the area’s Confederated Tribes of Siletz Indians support this belief. ______ Siletz stories describe how blocks of beeswax, an item the ship had been carrying, began washing ashore after the ship was lost.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For this reason,
choices.B: For example,
choices.C: However,
choices.D: Likewise,

explanation: The beeswax detail is a specific instance of the Siletz stories that support the belief, so an exemplifying transition fits. 'For this reason' and 'Likewise' misstate the relationship.

passage.t: Alexander Lawrence Posey (1873–1908) varied his focus and tone depending on the genre in which he was writing. In his poetry, he used heartfelt language to evoke the beauty and peacefulness of his natural surroundings; in his journalism, ______ he employed humor and satire to comment on political issues affecting his Muskogee Creek community.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: that is,
choices.B: granted,
choices.C: similarly,
choices.D: by contrast,

explanation: His poetry's heartfelt tone is set against his journalism's humor and satire—a direct contrast, signaled by the semicolon structure. 'Similarly' would claim they match.

passage.t: Geoscientists have long considered Hawaii’s Mauna Loa volcano to be Earth’s largest shield volcano by volume, measuring approximately 74,000 cubic kilometers. ______ according to a 2020 study by local geoscientist Michael Garcia, Hawaii’s Pūhāhonu shield volcano is significantly larger, boasting a volume of about 148,000 cubic kilometers.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Secondly,
choices.B: Consequently,
choices.C: Moreover,
choices.D: However,

explanation: The 2020 study overturns the long-held view that Mauna Loa is largest, so a contrast transition is required. 'Moreover' and 'Consequently' signal addition or cause.

passage.t: Okot p’Bitek’s poem Song of Lawino (1966) explores postcolonial Ugandan life through the eyes of a woman living in a rural village. With its vibrant imagery, bitingly satiric tone, and dexterous use of traditional Acholi song and phraseology, the poem inspired a generation of East African writers. ______ those who adopted its style are often referred to as Okot School poets.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: Fittingly,
choices.C: By comparison,
choices.D: Instead,

explanation: The name 'Okot School poets' aptly matches the poem's influence just described, so a transition signaling appropriateness fits. 'Nevertheless' and 'Instead' would signal contrast.

passage.t: Before the 1847 introduction of the US postage stamp, the cost of postage was usually paid by the recipient of a letter rather than the sender, and recipients were not always able or willing to pay promptly. ______ collecting this fee could be slow and arduous, and heaps of unpaid-for, undeliverable mail piled up in post offices.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Regardless,
choices.B: On the contrary,
choices.C: Consequently,
choices.D: For example,

explanation: Slow, arduous collection follows from recipients being unable or unwilling to pay, so a cause-effect transition is required.

passage.t: A potter choosing which type of clay to use for a piece considers two key factors: the desired look of the piece and its intended use. ______ earthenware clay is often used for decorative pieces because of its rustic look. This type of clay is not often used in industrial settings, though, because it is less durable than other clays.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In other words,
choices.B: Regardless,
choices.C: In conclusion,
choices.D: For example,

explanation: Earthenware clay is one illustration of the two factors just named, so an exemplifying transition fits. 'In other words' would signal restatement, and 'In conclusion' a summary.

passage.t: In Gothic architecture, flying buttresses are large arches that help support a building’s exterior walls. Before the Gothic era, cathedrals’ heavy ceilings had to be supported by thick, short walls, but the invention of flying buttresses eliminated this need. ______ Gothic cathedrals could be built with thinner, higher walls.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Similarly,
choices.B: For instance,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: As a result,

explanation: Thinner, higher walls are the consequence of buttresses eliminating the need for thick ones, so a cause-effect transition is required.

passage.t: Tyrian purple was a highly prized dye among the Phoenicians (an ancient civilization located in present-day Lebanon). The Phoenicians were famous for using this natural dye to color their clothes a distinctive purple. ______ the name “Phoenicia” itself, some historians claim, may have originally meant “land of purple.”

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In fact,
choices.B: Regardless,
choices.C: Lastly,
choices.D: On the contrary,

explanation: The etymology of 'Phoenicia' intensifies the point about how strongly they were associated with purple, so 'In fact' fits. 'Regardless' and 'On the contrary' both signal opposition.

passage.t: Etched into Peru’s Nazca Desert are line drawings so large that they can only be fully seen from high above.

Archaeologists have known of the lines since the 1920s, when a researcher spotted some from a nearby foothill, and they have been studying the markings ever since. ______ archaeologists’ efforts are aided by drones that capture high-resolution aerial photographs of the lines.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Currently,
choices.B: In comparison,
choices.C: Still,
choices.D: However,

explanation: The sentence shifts from the ongoing history of study to what is happening now with drones, so a present-time transition fits. 'Still' and 'However' would signal contrast.

passage.t: Because an achiral molecule is symmetrical, flipping it yields a structurally identical molecule. A flipped chiral molecule, ______ can be compared to a glove that has been turned inside out: it produces a structurally inverted molecule rather than an identical one.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: in other words,
choices.B: by contrast,
choices.C: for example,
choices.D: similarly,

explanation: Achiral molecules yield identical copies when flipped; chiral molecules yield inverted ones—a direct contrast. 'Similarly' and 'in other words' would claim agreement or restatement.

passage.t: Most conifers (trees belonging to the phylum Coniferophyta)are evergreen. That is, they keep their green leaves or needles year-round. However, not all conifer species are evergreen. Larch trees, ______ lose their needles every fall.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: for instance,
choices.B: nevertheless,
choices.C: meanwhile,
choices.D: in addition,

explanation: Larch trees illustrate the just-stated exception that not all conifers are evergreen, so an exemplifying transition is needed.

passage.t: Jhumpa Lahiri’s story collection Interpreter of Maladies features multiple stories about romantic relationships. choices.A: In the first place,
choices.B: On the other hand,
choices.C: For this reason,
choices.D: In comparison,

explanation: Gliding to conserve energy is the seal's response to the energy-versus-oxygen problem just described, so a cause-effect transition is required.

passage.t: In the early 1900s, Jovita Idár fought injustice on both sides of the Mexico–United States border. As a reporter for the Texas newspaper La Crónica, she voiced support for the Mexican people’s revolt against authoritarian rule. ______ she founded the League of Mexican Women, a group that advocated for the rights of Mexican Americans.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Additionally,
choices.B: In conclusion,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: Rather,

explanation: Founding the League is a second action beyond her reporting, so an additive transition fits. 'For example' would make it an instance of the reporting.

passage.t: To explore how blinking affects social interactions, Dutch researchers observed interactions between human speakers and “listeners” (animated human faces on a screen). The researchers found that when the listeners blinked slowly, the speakers tended to talk for less time. ______ quicker blinks were associated with longer talking times.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For example,
choices.B: Specifically,
choices.C: Firstly,
choices.D: By contrast,

explanation: Quick blinks produce the opposite result from slow blinks, so a contrast transition is required.

passage.t: In November 1934, Amrita Sher-Gil was living in what must have seemed like the ideal city for a young artist: Paris. She was studying firsthand the color-saturated style of France’s modernist masters and beginning to make a name for herself as a painter. ______ Sher-Gil longed to return to her childhood home of India; only there, she believed, could her art truly flourish.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Still,
choices.B: Therefore,
choices.C: Indeed,
choices.D: Furthermore,

explanation: Despite thriving in Paris, she longed to leave—a reversal of the expectation just built. 'Therefore,' 'Indeed,' and 'Furthermore' all signal agreement.

passage.t: In 1885, Chinese-born California resident Mary Tape became a hero of the Asian American civil rights movement. In January of that year, she won an antidiscrimination case in the California Supreme Court. ______ in April, she wrote an open letter criticizing her local board of education for discrimination. Both actions are remembered today as historic stands against racism.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Later,
choices.B: For instance,
choices.C: In other words,
choices.D: Rather,

explanation: The April letter follows the January court victory, so a time-sequence transition is needed. Both are separate historic actions, not examples of one another.

passage.t: When designing costumes for film, American artist Suttirat Larlarb typically custom fits the garments to each actor. ______ for the film Sunshine, in which astronauts must reignite a dying Sun, she designed a golden spacesuit and had a factory reproduce it in a few standard sizes; lacking a tailor-made quality, the final creations reflected the ungainliness of actual spacesuits.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Nevertheless,
choices.B: Thus,
choices.C: Likewise,
choices.D: Moreover,

explanation: The Sunshine spacesuits depart from her usual custom-fitting practice, so a contrast transition is required. 'Thus' and 'Likewise' would signal consequence or agreement.

passage.t: During a 2021 launch, Rocket Labs’ Electron rocket experienced an unexpected failure: its second-stage booster shut down suddenly after ignition. ______ instead of downplaying the incident, Rocket Labs’ CEO publicly acknowledged what happened and apologized for the loss of the rocket’s payload, which had consisted of two satellites.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Afterward,
choices.B: Additionally,
choices.C: Indeed,
choices.D: Similarly,

explanation: The CEO's response comes after the failure just described, so a time transition fits. 'Additionally,' 'Indeed,' and 'Similarly' do not mark that sequence.

passage.t: In 1891, dancer and choreographer Loie Fuller first performed her celebrated Serpentine Dance, artfully twirling her long, flowing skirt to create striking visual effects. ______ in 1896, cinema pioneers Auguste and Louis Lumière made a groundbreaking short film of Fuller’s dance.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: However,
choices.B: In conclusion,
choices.C: Later,
choices.D: In other words,

explanation: The 1896 film follows the 1891 performance, so a later-time transition is required.

passage.t: Phytoplankton play a crucial role in the ocean’s uptake of carbon from the atmosphere. When alive, these tiny marine organisms absorb atmospheric carbon via photosynthesis. ______ after they die, the phytoplankton sink to the seafloor, where the carbon in their cells gets stored in sediment, preventing it from cycling back into the atmosphere.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Specifically,
choices.B: By contrast,
choices.C: Nevertheless,
choices.D: Then,

explanation: What happens after the phytoplankton die is the next stage in the carbon-uptake process, so a sequencing transition fits. 'By contrast' would set the two stages in opposition rather than in order.

passage.t: Riley Black—the author of critically acclaimed books such as My Beloved Brontosaurus (2013)—is best known for writing about dinosaurs, but she has also conducted hands-on fieldwork. ______ her fieldwork has included paleontological digs in Utah, Montana, and Wyoming, and her dinosaur fossil discoveries can be seen at places such as the Carnegie Museum of Natural History.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Regardless,
choices.B: Subsequently,
choices.C: Specifically,
choices.D: Conversely,

explanation: The digs and discoveries spell out what her 'hands-on fieldwork' consisted of, so a narrowing transition is required.

passage.t: The Sun and other stars are powered by nuclear fusion reactions, in which two atoms collide to form a single heavier atom, releasing energy. Scientists have long believed that fusion has the potential to meet humanity’s clean energy needs. ______ prior to December 2022, no fusion reaction in a laboratory setting had ever generated a net energy gain.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: For this reason,
choices.B: Moreover,
choices.C: Specifically,
choices.D: That said,

explanation: The pre-2022 failure to achieve net energy gain qualifies the optimism just expressed, so a concessive transition is required. 'For this reason' and 'Moreover' misstate the relationship.

passage.t: “Wishcycling”—putting nonrecyclable items into recycling bins under the mistaken belief that those items can be recycled—ultimately does more harm than good. Nonrecyclable items, such as greasy pizza boxes, can contaminate recyclable materials, rendering entire batches unusable. ______ nonrecyclable products can damage recycling plants’ machinery.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Fittingly,
choices.B: On the contrary,
choices.C: Moreover,
choices.D: Nevertheless,

explanation: Machinery damage is a second harm beyond contaminated batches, so an additive transition fits.

passage.t: At two weeks old, the time their critical socialization period begins, wolves can smell but cannot yet see or hear. Domesticated dogs, ______ can see, hear, and smell by the end of two weeks. This relative lack of sensory input may help explain why wolves behave so differently around humans than dogs do: from a very young age, wolves are more wary and less exploratory.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: in other words,
choices.B: for instance,
choices.C: by contrast,
choices.D: accordingly,

explanation: Dogs' senses at two weeks are set against wolves' lack of sight and hearing, so a contrast transition is required.

passage.t: To discover which fruit varieties were grown in Italy’s Umbria region before the introduction of industrial farming, botanist Isabella Dalla Ragione often turns to centuries-old lists of cooking ingredients. ______ she analyzes Renaissance paintings of Umbria, as they can provide accurate representations of fruits that were grown there long ago.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: In sum,
choices.B: Instead,
choices.C: Thus,
choices.D: Additionally,

explanation: Analyzing paintings is a second source she uses beyond the ingredient lists, so an additive transition fits. 'Instead' would replace the first method.

passage.t: Laetitia Ky’s hair is her art. Inspired by hairstyles from various African tribes, the Ivorian artist uses wire and thread to sculpt her hair into all kinds of shapes. ______ she once made her hair into the shape of the continent of Africa— including the island of Madagascar!

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?

choices.A: Soon,
choices.B: Elsewhere,
choices.C: For example,
choices.D: However,

explanation: The Africa-shaped hairstyle illustrates the 'all kinds of shapes' just mentioned, so an exemplifying transition is needed.

x° and 72° are vertical angles at the point where t crosses p, and vertical angles are equal, so x = 72. The parallel line r isn't needed. Choice A would come from treating them as supplementary and halving.

Since m and n are parallel, the 170° angle at m and w° at n are corresponding angles across the transversal t, so w = 170. Choice A comes from treating them as supplementary, which applies to the other pair.
The 110° angle at C is exterior, so ∠BCA = 180 − 110 = 70°. Since ∠BAC equals ∠BCA, it is 70° too. The three angles sum to 180°, so x = 180 − 70 − 70 = 40. Choice B stops at ∠BCA.
Lines g and h are parallel, so x° and 175° are corresponding angles across the transversal and are therefore equal. x = 175.
Lines r and s are parallel, so x° and 162° are corresponding angles formed by the transversal n, making them equal. x = 162.

When two lines cross, the angles opposite each other are vertical angles and are equal. So z = w = 136. Choice B comes from subtracting w from 180, which applies to adjacent angles rather than opposite ones.
The angles of a triangle sum to 180°, and one is the right angle: a = 180 − 90 − 13 = 77. Choice D subtracts 13 from 90 and then adds, and A simply repeats the 13°.
PQ = QR makes the triangle isosceles, so the angles opposite those sides — at P and at R — are equal. Since ∠P = 24°, x = 24. You can check it: 132 + 24 + 24 = 180.

An equilateral triangle has all three sides equal. AB and BC are both 4,680 mm, so AC must also be 4,680 mm. The other choices give a third side of a different length, which would make the triangle isosceles at best.

BC and AD are parallel and line t cuts across both, so x° and y° are alternate interior angles — the angle at C and the angle at A on opposite sides of t. Alternate interior angles are equal, so y = 22. Choice B doubles it, and D takes the supplement.
In congruent triangles corresponding angles are equal, and E corresponds to J. So ∠J = ∠E = 45°. Choice A uses ∠F, which corresponds to K rather than J.

Lines ℓ and k are parallel, so a° and the 64° angle are co-interior across the transversal and sum to 180°. That gives a = 180 − 64 = 116. Choice B takes them as equal, which holds for the corresponding pair instead.

Two lines are parallel when a transversal makes a pair of corresponding angles equal. w° and the 40° angle sit in matching positions at j and at k, so w = 40 establishes j ∥ k. Choice C uses y°, which is at k on the other side and equal to 40° regardless of whether the lines are parallel.
Vertical angles are equal by definition, so angle 2 has the same measure as angle 1: 72°. Choice B gives the supplement, 180 − 72, which describes an adjacent angle rather than the vertical one.
The angles of a triangle sum to 180°, and x° is the remaining angle once y and z are accounted for: x = 180 − 20 − 60 = 100. Choice A adds y and z instead of subtracting their sum from 180.

Because m and n are parallel, x° and 26° are co-interior angles — on the same side of the transversal, between the two lines — so they sum to 180°. That gives x = 180 − 26 = 154. Choice B treats them as corresponding, which would make them equal.
The three angles sum to 180°, so ∠S and ∠T together take up 180 − 63 = 117°. ∠S must therefore be less than 117°, and 116 is the only choice that fits. Choice B at 118 already exceeds what's left.

With m parallel to n, the 134° angle and w° are corresponding angles across the transversal t, so they are equal: w = 134. Choice C comes from subtracting from 180, which applies to the co-interior pair.
AB = AC makes the triangle isosceles, so ∠ACB equals ∠ABC = 67°. The angles sum to 180°, so x = 180 − 67 − 67 = 46. Choice A subtracts only one 67° and then halves.
The angles of a triangle sum to 180°: ∠Z = 180 − 24 − 98 = 58°. Choice B subtracts 24 from 98, and D adds the two given angles.
Lines s and t are parallel, so x° and 110° are co-interior angles across the transversal c and sum to 180°. That gives x = 180 − 110 = 70.

Two lines cut by a transversal are parallel exactly when a pair of corresponding angles is equal. The 24° angle at r and x° at s sit in matching positions, so x = 24 is what establishes r ∥ s. Choices A and C allow the lines to converge or diverge.
In right triangle PQR the angles are 90°, 18° and ∠P, so ∠P = 180 − 90 − 18 = 72°. Similar triangles have equal corresponding angles, and P corresponds to S, so ∠S = 72°. Choice A copies ∠Q instead.
r° and s° are vertical angles — opposite each other where the two lines cross — so they are equal: s = 53. Choice C takes the supplement, 180 − 53, which describes the adjacent angle.

AD and BE are straight lines crossing at C, so x° and y° are adjacent angles along a straight line and sum to 180°. That gives y = 180 − 100 = 80. Choice A treats them as vertical angles, which would make them equal.

Dilation changes size but not shape, so corresponding angles are unchanged no matter the scale factor. Angle X corresponds to angle A, which is 60°, so ∠X = 60°. Choices A and B apply the scale factor of 3 to the angle, which only affects lengths.
The three angles sum to 180°, so ∠J and ∠K together measure 180 − 118 = 62°. Since they are equal, each is 62 ÷ 2 = 31°. Choice C stops at 62 without halving.
The angles of a triangle sum to 180°: ∠A = 180 − 52 − 17 = 111°. Choice C subtracts the two given angles from each other and B from 52.
The angles of a triangle sum to 180°: ∠Z = 180 − 23 − 66 = 91°. Choice A subtracts 23 from 66, and B adds the two given angles.

c is the hypotenuse, so by the Pythagorean theorem c² = 9² + 6² = 81 + 36 = 117, giving c = √117 ≈ 10.8. Choice C adds the legs, which always overshoots, and D adds their squares without taking the root.

Tangent is opposite over adjacent. From the angle x° at the top, the opposite leg is the base of 26 and the adjacent leg is the vertical side of 7, so tan x° = 26/7. Choice A inverts the ratio, which would be tan of the other acute angle.

Sine is opposite over hypotenuse. From x° the opposite side is 63 and the hypotenuse — the side across from the right angle — is 73, so sin x° = 63/73. Choice A uses 73/63, putting the hypotenuse on top.

The right angle is between the legs 4 and b, so 19 is the hypotenuse. The Pythagorean theorem gives 4² + b² = 19². Choice D subtracts, which would apply if b were the hypotenuse, and A and B add the lengths themselves rather than their squares.

Similar triangles have equal corresponding angles, and B corresponds to E. Since ∠E = ∠B, their cosines are identical, so cos E takes the same value as cos B. The scale factor between the triangles affects lengths, never angles.

c is the hypotenuse, so c² = a² + b² and c = √(4² + 5²). Choice C takes the root of the sum of the lengths instead of the sum of their squares, and A adds the legs, which always overshoots the hypotenuse.
The two legs meet at the right angle and c is the hypotenuse, so the Pythagorean theorem gives 12² + 3² = c². Choice D subtracts, and B adds the lengths rather than their squares.
The hypotenuse is √(3² + 7²) = √(9 + 49) = √58 ≈ 7.6. Choice B is 3 + 7 − 5, and D adds the squares without taking the root. Note the hypotenuse must exceed 7, the longer leg, which rules out A.
